properties.areaDesc: Coconino, AZ
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 4 at 4:57AM MST until November 4 at 7:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Moenkopi Wash near Tuba City in Coconino County...

* WHEN...Until 700 PM MST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of Moenkopi Wash is occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 453 AM MST, water levels are continue to gradually fall this
morning, though remain above moderate flood stage. The water is
forecast to eventually fall below flood stage by late Wednesday
afternoon.
- Flooding is occurring along Moenkopi Wash.
- For Moenkopi Wash at Moenkopi Wash Near Tuba City:
At 3:45am MST the stage was 28.32 feet.
Flood Stage is 27.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 27.73 feet is expected at 5:00am MST
Wednesday.
Impacts:
At 27.0 feet: At 27.0 feet water begins to encroach on homes in
lower Moenkopi Village and floods crop fields along the river.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Moenkopi.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will be dangerous. Do not attempt to cross
flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 7 PM MST THIS EVENING

properties.areaDesc: Clay, NE; Fillmore, NE; Hamilton, NE; Merrick, NE; Nance, NE; Polk, NE; York, NE
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 4 at 5:32AM CST until November 4 at 3:00PM CST by NWS Hastings NE
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall on Monday and Tuesday
continues.

* WHERE...Merrick County in central Nebraska...
Nance County in central Nebraska...
Polk County in east central Nebraska...
York County in east central Nebraska...
Northern Clay County in south central Nebraska...
Northwestern Fillmore County in south central Nebraska...
Hamilton County in south central Nebraska...

* WHEN...Until 300 PM CST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of several smaller creeks, streams, and other
low-lying and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring, along
with possible flooding along a few area rivers. Numerous rural
roads likely remain in very poor condition.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 524 AM CST, Various reports along with data from automated
river gauges indicated that mainly minor flooding continues
within various parts of the Warning area, due to a widespread 2-5
inches of rain that fell from Monday into Tuesday. Although
excess water will continue to gradually recede from rural roads
and low-lying areas now that rain has ended and most of the next
several days will be dry, minor flooding will remain possible for
at least another day or two especially along smaller creeks and
streams in the area, along with perhaps a few smaller rivers.
Automated gauges indicate that minor flooding is possible over
the next few days, mainly along the Silver Creek and Prairie
Creek in Merrick and Nance counties, and also along the West Fork
Big Blue River in portions of Hamilton, Fillmore and York
counties...including the McCool Junction area. Early this
morning, the automated gauge on the Silver Creek near Silver
Creek has reached its flood stage of 9 feet, and the gauge on the
West Fork Big Blue River near Grafton is within 1 foot of its
flood stage of 11 feet.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Galaway Creek, North Branch Big Blue River, Prairie Slough,
Beaver Creek, Wood River, Stone Creek, Prairie Creek, West Fork
Big Blue River, Lincoln Creek, Timber Creek, School Creek, Clear
Creek, Cottonwood Creek, Plum Creek, Elk Creek, Dry Run Creek,
Warm Slough, Moores Creek.
- Some locations that could experience flooding include...
York, Aurora, Central City, Fullerton, Stromsburg, Harvard,
Genoa, Henderson, Osceola, Shelby, Palmer, Hampton, McCool
Junction, Clarks, Silver Creek, Giltner, Polk, Chapman, Phillips
and Bradshaw.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.description:
Updated to clean up zone splits

...COASTAL FLOOD STATEMENT REMAINS IN EFFECT...

* WHAT...Minor saltwater flooding.

* WHERE...Middle and Upper Florida Keys.

* WHEN...Through Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...Minor saltwater flooding of low elevation streets
and lots is likely. Some storm drains will overflow, and some
seawalls and docks will be overtopped. Boaters can expect less
clearance under fixed bridges. Motorists should remember that
persistent puddles around the times of high tide are almost
certain to contain a mix of saltwater.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.description:

currents with breaking waves of 12 to 16 ft expected.

* WHERE...Pacific Coast beaches.

* WHEN...From 5 AM Thursday to 7 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Waves can sweep across the shoreline without

properties.instruction:

and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,

properties.areaDesc: Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 4 at 12:33AM PST until November 9 at 1:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.6 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, an increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 12 to 16 ft expected.

* WHERE...Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 6 AM this morning to
1 PM PST Monday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, from 5 AM
Thursday to 7 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high
tide is expected to be 1.0 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at
8:00 AM Wednesday 11/4, 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at
8:35 AM Thursday 11/5, 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at
9:08 AM Friday 11/6, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 9:38
AM Saturday 11/7, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 10:06
AM Sunday 11/8, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 10:35 AM
Monday 11/9. These predictions include up to 1.2 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 3 at 7:52PM EST until November 5 at 10:00AM EST by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Manatee River Near Myakka Head at SR 64 affecting Manatee County.

Peace River At Zolfo Springs at SR 17 affecting Hardee County.

Alafia River At Lithia affecting Hillsborough County.

Peace River At Arcadia at SR 70 affecting DeSoto County.

Horse Creek Near Arcadia at SR 72 affecting DeSoto County.

.Heavy rain of 5 to 10 inches across portions of west central Florida
caused several rivers across the region to remain in flood stage over
the next few days.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Peace River at Zolfo Springs at SR 17.

* WHEN...Until Thursday morning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Tuesday the stage was 16.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 14.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Tuesday was 16.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage early
Thursday morning and continue falling to 13.6 feet Friday
evening.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 16.6
feet on 01/26/1958.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday morning at 1100 AM EST.

properties.areaDesc: Coconino, AZ; Navajo, AZ
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 3 at 5:25PM MST until November 4 at 10:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...The Little Colorado River from Winslow to Leupp...

* WHEN...Until 1000 AM MST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Little Colorado River is occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 518 PM MST, the guage on the Little Colorado River at Winslow
had dropped below moderate flood stage. Water levels are forecast
to continue gradually drop, eventually falling below flood stage
by late Wednesday afternoon.
- For the Little Colorado River at Winslow:
At 5:00pm MST the stage was 21.74 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Forecast: Water levels are forecast to continue to fall, falling
below flood stage by late Wednesday afternoon.
Impacts:
At 19.0 feet: Overflow on right bank. Water approaches Ames Acres
and Bushman Acres on left bank in Winslow area. Erosion is likely
on the levee on the left bank. Downstream, with approximately 18
hour lag time, the approaches to the bridge over the river on
Navajo Route 71 near Bird Springs will flood and evacuations of
homes near the intersection of Navajo Route 2 and Navajo Route 71
are conducted.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Winslow, Leupp, Birdsprings, Sunrise, Bushman Acres, Homolovi
Ruins State Park and Clear Creek Reservoir.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will be dangerous. Do not attempt to cross
flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 10 AM MST WEDNESDAY

properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow and blowing snow expected. Total snow accumulations up
to two inches. Winds gusting as high as 35 to 50 mph.

* WHERE...Central Beaufort Sea Coast, Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast, and
Northern Arctic Coast.

* WHEN...From midnight tonight to 3 PM AKST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Areas of blowing snow could
reduce visibility below one half mile. Blizzard conditions will be
possible dependent on the severity of blowing snow.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds will steadily ramp up Tuesday night and
throughout the day Wednesday. Strongest winds will be immediately
along the coast, with lighter winds farther inland. This will be a
long duration wind event, with gusty winds expected to continue
through the weekend.
properties.instruction: Slow down and use caution while traveling.

properties.areaDesc: Alamosa, CO; Conejos, CO; Costilla, CO
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 3:53PM MST until November 4 at 4:00PM MST by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
Flooding along the Conejos River and San Antonio River continues.

* WHAT...Flooding along the Conejos River and San Antonio River,
caused by recent runoff from upstream rain and snowmelt, is
occurring.

* WHERE...Eastern Conejos County in south central Colorado...
West Central Costilla County in south central Colorado...
South Central Alamosa County in southeastern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 400 PM MST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding along the Conejos River, from Mogote downstream
to Manassa, and the San Antonio River, near Ortiz downstream to
Manassa, is ongoing. Additional flooding of creeks, streams, and
other low-lying and flood-prone locations is possible. Numerous
roads remain closed due to flooding. Expect many areas of slow
moving or standing water through eastern Conejos County.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 347 PM MST, Upstream runoff from recent rain and snowmelt is
causing flooding into eastern Conejos County.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Manassa, Sanford, Antonito, Romeo, Alamosa East, Conejos and
Ortiz.
- http://www.water.noaa.gov
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 3:29PM MST until November 6 at 12:00AM MST by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Pueblo has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in Colorado...

Rio Grande At Alamosa affecting Alamosa County.

.Minor flooding along the Rio Grande through Alamosa is expected due
to upstream flooding occurring in the vicinity of Monte Vista.

For the Rio Grande...including Alamosa...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Alamosa.

* WHEN...From Wednesday afternoon to late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Minor flooding. Minor agricultural flooding
in low lying areas along the river.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:30 PM MST Monday the stage was 2.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage early
Wednesday afternoon to a crest of 9.6 feet late Wednesday
evening. It will then fall below flood stage early Thursday
afternoon.
- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.
- http://www.water.noaa.gov
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

This warning will be in effect until the river falls below its flood
stage.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at water.noaa.gov.

The next statement will be issued Thursday morning at 1100 AM MST.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING IN EFFECT FROM WEDNESDAY AFTERNOON TO LATE THURSDAY NIGHT... ...REPLACES RIVER FLOOD WATCH

properties.areaDesc: Montezuma, CO; San Juan, UT
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 12:31PM MST until November 5 at 5:15PM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding along the San Juan River caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...along the San Juan River from the Four Corners through
Mexican Hat, UT. This includes Bluff, Montezuma Creek and Aneth.

* WHEN...Until 515 PM MST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...River levels continue to rise due to excess runoff from
Sunday's rainfall. Expect high water levels and the River exceeding
its banks, inundating low-lying areas along the San Juan River. A
prolonged period of high water is forecast, with a crest near 23.5
ft Thursday morning. It will take several hours for all the water
from these storms to work through local drainage systems.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1222 PM MST, stream gauge reports upstream and impacts of
flooding have been reported along the San Juan River near
Farmington, NM. Expect flood waters to reach the Four Corners
Wednesday evening and the town of Bluff early Thursday morning.
Timing of crest is subject to change as more details become
available. Please continue to monitor the forecast and updated
warnings.
- At 11:30 AM MST Monday the stage was 20.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 22.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise to 22 feet late this evening with
a secondary crest near 23.5 feet expected near Bluff early
Thursday morning. It will then fall below flood stage Thursday
morning.
- Flood stage is 23.0 feet.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mexican Hat, Bluff, Montezuma Creek, and Aneth.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
